readings: In the scanqc table, count the QC records (rows) under each archival status (`archstat`), with a NULL status treated as its own group. Compute each status's share as its record count divided by the sum of the record counts over all statuses. Return only the statuses whose share is above the average share across statuses. Show the status, the record count, the share, and the share minus the average share, with no rounding.

In the scanqc table, count the distinct projects (distinct `arcref`) under each archival status (`archstat`), with a NULL status treated as its own group. A project with QC records under several statuses is counted once in each of those statuses. Compute each status's share as its distinct-project count divided by the sum of the distinct-project counts over all statuses. Return only the statuses whose share is above the average share across statuses. Show the status, the distinct-project count, the share, and the share minus the average share, with no rounding.
queries:
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT archstat, COUNT(*) AS record_count
  FROM scanqc
  GROUP BY archstat
),
shares AS (
  SELECT archstat, record_count,
         record_count * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(record_count) FROM counts) AS share
  FROM counts
),
avg_share AS (
  SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares
)
SELECT s.archstat, s.record_count, s.share, s.share - a.avg_share AS share_minus_avg
FROM shares s, avg_share a
WHERE s.share > a.avg_share;
WITH s AS (
  SELECT archstat, COUNT(DISTINCT arcref) AS cnt
  FROM scanqc
  GROUP BY archstat
),
t AS (
  SELECT archstat, cnt, CAST(cnt AS REAL) / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM s) AS share
  FROM s
),
a AS (
  SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM t
)
SELECT t.archstat, t.cnt AS distinct_project_count, t.share, t.share - a.avg_share AS share_minus_avg
FROM t, a
WHERE t.share > a.avg_share;
